key_drivers: Three consecutive double-digit declines on the print: -13.0% (2025-11-26), -12.2% (2026-02-27), -31.5% (2026-05-27), computed from Yahoo daily bars. Every one was a guidance event, not a miss on actuals

Tonight is the first FORMAL FY2027 guide. In May management pre-signalled a 16-17% ARR/revenue framework against a ~25% run rate and the stock lost 31%. For the stock to rally, a team that has just lost two senior sales leaders under the CRO has to guide its opening annual number ABOVE its own conservative framework - the opposite of its established practice

The cushion has been spent. ZS is +15.0% over the past month and +2.8% today, having jumped ~10% into the report on a JPMorgan target hike and a broad cybersecurity re-rating after strong CRWD and PANW prints. Low expectations were the bull case and they have been partly re-priced away
Evercore cut the stock to a tactical underperform into the print, flagging how long the growth rate can last against Netskope, Cato Networks and Palo Alto
Options price ~13% and the realised move has exceeded the implied in 5 of the last 8 reports, so the straddle is not obviously expensive relative to the delivered distribution
what_would_change_my_mind: An opening FY2027 ARR or revenue guide meaningfully above the 16-17% framework, or evidence that the Q4 sales-leadership transition did not dent net new ARR.
reasoning: The market's read is that the bar is already on the floor after May's 31% collapse, and that CRWD/PANW proved AI is lifting security demand. That is why the stock has added 15% in a month. But the thing that broke ZS three quarters running was never the quarter being reported - it was the forward number, and tonight produces the largest forward number of the year. A management team that took two senior sales departures at the close of Q3 and responded by framing FY27 at 16-17% is not the team that raises above its own framework eight weeks later. The pre-print rally has removed the disappointment cushion that would otherwise have made this a coin flip. Modest conviction only: the reset is real and a clean beat with an in-line FY27 guide could relieve.

key_drivers: Recent print reactions run strongly positive and large: +17.4% (2025-09-05), +11.1% (2025-12-05), +19.5% (2026-03-06), computed from Yahoo daily bars. The one big negative, -15.6% (2025-03-07), is now six quarters back

Q1 FY2027 was a clean beat-and-raise: revenue $479m, +31% y/y against a $455m consensus, adjusted EPS $0.17 vs $0.13, third consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability, FY2027 revenue guide raised to $2.005-2.013bn

Unlike GWRE, PATH and DOCU tonight, there is almost no run-in to unwind: +3.3% over the past month and still -14% over 52 weeks, at $38.35 against a 52-week high of $47.47. Whatever happens, it is not happening from a stretched base
The Q2 bar is undemanding on its face: consensus $0.16 and ~$483m against company guidance of $0.15-0.16
The offsetting risk is valuation, not execution - P/E above 400 - plus roughly $159.5m of insider selling over three months and a large institutional stake reduction
what_would_change_my_mind: ARR growth decelerating below the high-20s, or any softening in the FY2027 revenue guide raised in June.
reasoning: The only name tonight where a consistently positive reaction history meets a setup that has not already rallied into the print. Samsara has beaten and raised repeatedly, turned GAAP profitable three quarters running, and is compounding ARR near 30% - and the stock is still a third below its 52-week high with a flat month behind it. The bear case is entirely multiple, not business: over 400x earnings and heavy insider selling, in a tape where high-multiple software sold off today on rising yields and Iran headlines. That is a real cap on the upside and the reason this is Lean and not Strong. But a beat-and-raise from a de-rated position is the shape that produced +17% and +19% moves in this name twice in the last year.

key_drivers: Two strong forces point opposite ways and I cannot rank them. Seasonal: the fiscal Q4 print is Guidewire's good one - +20.1% (2025-09-05) and +12.4% (2024-09-06) - because it carries the opening FY ARR guide off the year's biggest ARR quarter
Against that, the run-in is the largest of any name tonight bar PATH: +28.0% over the past month, from ~$157 to $201.46, and the last print went the other way at -10.0% (2026-06-05)
The fundamental setup is genuinely good - fiscal 2026 ARR guided to $1.21-1.22bn on accelerating cloud migration and Tier 1 wins - which is precisely what the 28% already reflects

Consensus for the quarter is around $0.93 EPS on ~$403m revenue. Note the Nasdaq calendar carries $0.49, a different basis; I did not resolve which is GAAP and which is non-GAAP and have not relied on either
Still 26% below the 52-week high of $272.60, so the de-rating from the peak is not fully unwound even after the month's rally
what_would_change_my_mind: An opening FY2027 ARR guide clearly above or below the ~$1.4bn the current run rate and cloud pipeline imply would break the tie in the corresponding direction.
reasoning: Guidewire's fiscal Q4 has twice produced double-digit rallies because it is when the cloud-migration story gets quantified for the year ahead, and the business is executing. But the stock has already run 28% in a month into exactly that expectation, and the most recent print - Q3 in June - fell 10%. A high-quality company arriving at its best print of the year with a month of gains already banked is the definition of a two-sided setup: the good news is required rather than optional. I have no information that resolves which side wins, so I decline the direction and keep only the magnitude view, which is that this moves double digits either way.

key_drivers: An unbroken run of negative prints, several severe: -14.2% (2025-03-28), -19.8% (2025-06-06), -18.6% (2025-09-05), and ~-11% after the 2026-06-04 Q1 report, computed from Yahoo daily bars plus CNBC. The market has repeatedly failed to price how bad the guide would be, four quarters running

UBS told clients on 25 August it expects a SECOND fiscal 2026 EPS guidance cut, of roughly $1.25 to $9.70-9.90, on weak US and China sales, and cut its target to $120 - a target the stock is now trading at. Barclays cut to $113

The quarter itself is guided to shrink: revenue $2.45-2.475bn, -2% to -3% with North America down low double digits, EPS $1.76-1.81 against $3.10 a year ago, gross margin down 410bps on tariffs (150bps headwind, 100bps offset) and 50bps more markdowns
The China engine, the one growth leg left in the story, has stalled - and it was the offset management leaned on when North America first softened
The stock has bounced into the print rather than capitulating: ~$113 in late August to $119.15 now, so the setup is not washed out at the moment of the event even though it is -46% year to date
what_would_change_my_mind: A full-year guide left intact - no second cut - or any sign that North American comparable traffic has inflected, which would turn four quarters of over-punishment into a relief rally.
reasoning: The obvious objection is that a second guidance cut is consensus - UBS published the number - and the stock is already down 46% on the year, so it should be in the price. That objection has been available before each of the last four prints and has been wrong every time, by 14%, 20%, 19% and 11%. The pattern is that the market prices a cut and lululemon delivers a worse one, because the deterioration is compounding across regions rather than bottoming: North America down low double digits, China stalling, tariffs taking 150bps of gross margin, and markdowns rising as the brand reset works through inventory. What tips this from a base-rate call to a real one is that the stock rallied roughly 5% into the event off its late-August lows, so it arrives at the print with something to lose. Options price 9.9% against a 9.5% historical average; I take the history.

key_drivers: The run-in argues one way: +20.8% over the past month, from ~$55 to $66.61, putting the stock at the very top of the $41.37-66.78 range it has traded since the June print
The bar argues the other: consensus ~$1.08-1.09 EPS on ~$867m revenue, +8.3% y/y, against a company that has beaten on EPS repeatedly and guided FY2027 revenue to $3.490-3.502bn

Billings disclosure was discontinued from Q1 FY2027 in favour of ARR, which removes the single metric that caused the -19% and several other negative reactions - a structural change to the shape of the risk that I cannot yet handicap
Growth is only 8-9%, so this is a valuation-and-narrative stock, and the AI/IAM narrative is exactly what the last month's 21% rally has been paying for
what_would_change_my_mind: A first full-year ARR target that implies acceleration above 9%, or conversely any IAM adoption metric that undercuts the narrative the past month has priced.
reasoning: A 21% rally into the print at the top of the post-June range is a reason for caution, and on that alone I would lean down. What stops me is that DocuSign retired quarterly billings disclosure this fiscal year. Billings was the metric that produced the -19% and most of the other bad prints; with it gone and ARR not yet established as the thing the market trades on, I do not know what the sensitivity looks like any more. The reaction distribution is wide and symmetric, the fundamentals are unremarkable at 8-9% growth, and the valuation is neither cheap enough to floor it nor stretched enough to break it. No edge - I take the magnitude read only, at the lower end of tonight's set because the two most recent reactions were single digit.

key_drivers: The sharpest mismatch on the board between the stock and the business. PATH is +42.1% over the past month and at $18.54 against a 52-week high of $19.84 - while ARR grew 12% and net dollar retention was 109% in Q1

The rally is narrative, not numbers: agentic AI moving from pilot to production. Tonight the narrative has to produce ARR, and Q2 ARR is guided to $1.929-1.934bn, which is only about 1.5% sequential growth on the Q1 figure of $1.901bn
Consensus of ~$0.15 non-GAAP EPS on ~$397.85m revenue sits near the top of the company's own $395-400m guide, so an in-line quarter clears nothing that is not already required
The beat record is strong - 7 of the last 8 quarters on both lines - which is exactly why beating is not sufficient from here
Reaction history is wide and asymmetric to the downside when the story wobbles: +24.4% (2025-12-04) but -15.7% (2025-03-13) and -11.1% (2026-07-22)
what_would_change_my_mind: An ARR guide for the back half that inflects growth back toward the high teens, which would justify the re-rating rather than merely surviving it.
reasoning: A stock that has added 42% in a month arrives at its print needing the story to be confirmed rather than merely intact, and UiPath's underlying numbers are not keeping pace with the re-rating: 12% ARR growth, 109% net retention, and a Q2 ARR guide implying about 1.5% sequential progress. Agentic AI is a real product cycle and the company beats consistently, but a beat is the base case priced at $18.54 within 7% of the 52-week high. The most likely disappointment is not a bad quarter, it is a good quarter with an ARR guide that shows the agentic revenue is still small. Low conviction and a small score: I am reasoning from positioning rather than from anything specific about the quarter, and that is a thinner basis than the LULU or ZS calls.

key_drivers: By far the largest expected move of the day and not close. Every recent print has been violent in one direction or the other: +49.4% (2025-06-05), +47.9% (2025-09-08), +35.0% (2025-12-11), -26.0% (2026-06-05), -28.2% (2024-09-06)

The fundamentals point up: Q1 FY2027 revenue $94.2m, +42% y/y, EPS -$0.03 against -$0.04 expected, FY guidance raised to $425-441m, RPO ~$816m (+80% y/y) and estimated backlog ~$906m (+72% y/y), $731m cash

The tape points down: -15.7% over the past month and -9.3% today, on a seven-figure European defence award that read small next to the eight- and nine-figure contracts booked earlier this year, plus a sector-wide pullback across commercial space names on a day the broad market was up
Q2 is guided to $102-107m, ~42% growth at the midpoint, with adjusted EBITDA between breakeven and $5m - so the profitability inflection is live but thin enough to miss either way
Short-dated options activity into the print was reported as tilting defensive with traders positioned for a sharp move in either direction, which matches my read: high variance, no direction
what_would_change_my_mind: Nothing available before the close. The determinant is whether backlog converts to revenue at the guided pace and whether adjusted EBITDA lands positive, and neither is knowable from outside.
reasoning: Planet Labs is the clearest magnitude call and the least tractable direction call of the day. Three of the last five prints moved 35-49% up and two moved 26-28% down; there is no middle in this distribution. The business is genuinely accelerating - 42% growth, backlog up 72%, defence and intelligence revenue up 50% on sovereign European and NATO work - and the stock is down 36% in thirty days, which is the setup that produced the +47.9% print a year ago. But the same stock fell 26% on its last report with comparable fundamentals behind it, and today it dropped 9% because a defence award was too small, which tells me the marginal buyer is now sizing every headline against a very high bar. I take the variance and decline the direction.

key_drivers: The second-largest expected move tonight. Print reactions computed from Yahoo daily bars: -17.1% (2025-02-27), -15.1% (2025-05-30), +16.8% (2025-08-29), -18.8% (2025-11-26), -21.4% (2026-05-29). Ambarella essentially does not have small earnings days

Direction is a genuine coin flip and I checked this rather than assuming. A secondary source claimed five consecutive negative reactions averaging -9.8%; the bars say otherwise - the sequence alternates and includes a +16.8%, so there is no streak to follow
The one large positive in that sequence was the year-ago fiscal Q2, the same quarter reporting tonight, and management has guided Q2 FY2027 as seasonally strong at $105-111m against Q1's $100.4m

Against that, the stock is -20.0% over the past month at $66.15, closer to the 52-week low of $48.30 than to the high of $96.69 - the de-rating has already happened, which lowers the bar but also says something about what holders now expect
Q1 FY2027 was a beat, $100.4m revenue +16.9% y/y with a record automotive quarter, and it still fell 21% - so a beat is demonstrably not sufficient in this name
what_would_change_my_mind: A fiscal Q3 revenue guide clearly above the ~$115m the seasonal pattern implies would make this Lean Up; anything at or below Q2's midpoint would make it Lean Down.
reasoning: Ambarella moves 15-21% on almost every print, so the magnitude number is well anchored and high. Direction is where I stop. The temptation was a streak call - one source reported five straight double-digit declines - but recomputing from daily bars shows an alternating sequence with a +16.8% in it, and the +16.8% was the same fiscal Q2 that reports tonight, which management has guided as seasonally strong. So the seasonal read is mildly positive while the momentum read is negative, the stock having lost 20% in a month. The deciding evidence would be the fiscal Q3 guide and it does not exist yet. What I will note is the pattern that a 17% revenue beat in Q1 still produced a 21% decline: in this name the guide is everything and the actuals are noise, and I have no view on the guide.
